evals.prompt: Add a Project feature with create, get by id and filter. A project has a name unique per owner, a description and a status (Draft, Active, Completed, Archived). Only the owner can read it; admins can read every project. Add the SQL, the seed, the local Swagger examples and the tests. Finish with the repository gates.
evals.expected_output: A complete vertical slice: Domain entity/enum/constraints; Application input/validator/port/filter/sort catalog/DTO/handler with ValidatorSet; Infrastructure table/sort columns/ADO.NET repository over NpgsqlDataSource; SQL schema + seed; API request/response/endpoints/route group/module/JSON context/OpenAPI descriptors; local Swagger examples with seed-consistent bodies, parameters and responses; unit, component, functional and architecture tests, including sort alignment; README update; build, AOT publish, test and coverage results reported. The agent presents a plan first because the change adds a table and crosses layers.
expectations: The plan names every layer and the files it will touch before editing, and waits for confirmation because a table is added
Domain contains ProjectEntity, EProjectStatus and ProjectConstraints and references no outer layer

Application contains CreateProjectInput/Validator/Handler, GetProjectByIdInput/Validator/Handler, FilteredProjectInput/Validator/Handler, IProjectRepository, ProjectFilter, ProjectSortCatalog, ProjectDto and ProjectDtoExtensions

The handlers implement IHandler<TInput, TResult>, derive from ValidationService, take ValidatorSet<TInput>, return Result<T>, check NameExistsAsync before InsertAsync and return ConflictError for a duplicate
The API reports one AddUseCase per use case and one AddProjectModule call, not per-type registrations scattered through ConfigureServices
Infrastructure contains ProjectTable, ProjectSortColumns and ProjectRepository; every query value is a bound NpgsqlParameter and every identifier comes from ProjectTable
ProjectSortCatalog is the single accepted-key list; ProjectSortColumns maps it; ProjectSortColumnsTests asserts the two sets are equal
The SQL script creates the table with Id bytea, timestamptz audit columns and UX_Project_CreatedBy_Name; the seed uses the devtoken emails and covers every status
The module registers the repository, one AddUseCase per input, ProjectRoutes as IGroupMap, ProjectJsonSerializerContext and the OpenAPI transformer
local/openapi/examples.json has an entry for every Project operation, with bodies and responses that match the seed and users.json; route parameters use the array form
Create uses currentUser.Owner.OwnerForCreate; get and filter use currentUser.Owner.VisibleOwner or FilterOwners; no owner comes from the request body
The endpoint plumbing lives in ProjectEndpoints; ProjectRoutes keeps templates and metadata and does not inject ICurrentUser

Tests include validator tests, handler tests with ValidatorSet and NSubstitute, a sort-alignment test, component tests (201/400/409/200/404/204), an authorization matrix (401/403/2xx), a functional flow and a JSON contract test
Tests use [ResetDatabase], [AuthenticatedAs], TestData, ProjectBuilder and Eventually; no Thread.Sleep, Task.Delay, hardcoded id or login endpoint
The AOT publish was run and its result reported separately from the build
The final report lists the real commands and exit codes and does not claim a gate that did not run

evals.prompt: Add a component test for POST /api/todos that proves a duplicate name returns 409 and that the row is not inserted twice.
evals.expected_output: One component test class in the ComponentTests project, following the fixture, attributes, TestData and builder conventions. The test seeds a Todo, posts the same name as the same owner, asserts 409 and asserts the stored count is unchanged. The agent runs the test project and reports the result.
expectations: The test lives in tests/CleanWebApiTemplate.Api.ComponentTests/Todo (or the matching feature folder), not in UnitTests
The class derives from ComponentTestBase and uses the ComponentTestFixture
The test uses [ResetDatabase] and [AuthenticatedAs(TestUser.TodoUser)] on the method or class
The test seeds with Fixture.Todos.AddAsync(new TodoBuilder()...), not with raw SQL
The test posts to /api/todos/ with TestData.Unique or a fixed name and asserts HttpStatusCode.Conflict
The test asserts the row count or that only one row with that name exists
The test uses CancellationToken and has Arrange/Act/Assert
The agent ran dotnet test --project tests/CleanWebApiTemplate.Api.ComponentTests/... and reported the real result
The agent did not weaken BlockExternalHttpHandler or the authorization configuration to make the test pass

evals.prompt: Add a Priority column (Low, Normal, High) to Todo. It must be persisted, validated, exposed in the API, included in the seed, documented in OpenAPI and covered by tests.
evals.expected_output: A full column change: enum/constraints and entity in Domain; input/validator and DTO updates in Application; table constant, repository column list/mapping/parameters and SQL in Infrastructure/database; request/response and JSON/OpenAPI updates in Api; seed values; unit, component and OpenAPI tests; README update; gates.
expectations: The enum EPriority has explicit values starting at 1 and is used instead of raw integers in the domain/application contracts
The entity, input, DTO, request and response carry the new field; the create and update validators reject unknown values
TodoTable, the Columns list, the INSERT/UPDATE parameters, MapTodo and a new forward-only SQL script all include the column with consistent types
If Priority is sortable, TodoSortCatalog and TodoSortColumns both include it and TodoSortColumnsTests passes
The SQL default or seed covers every priority and does not violate a constraint
The JSON context and the OpenAPI schema describe the new field, including the allowed values
The local Swagger request/response examples include the new field and remain consistent with the seed
Unit tests cover the validator and handler; component tests cover create/read/update with the new field; the OpenAPI contract test asserts the schema
The agent ran the build, the AOT publish, the tests and coverage and reported real results
No reflection, dynamic, EF Core or Dapper was introduced

evals.prompt: Add a Reports role that can read every owner's projects but cannot create, update or delete them. Add it to the local profiles and the tests.
evals.expected_output: A new role and policy: Constants, ConfigureAuth policy, a route group or endpoint using it, TestUser/TestUsers definitions, devtoken and local OpenAPI users, an authorization matrix (401/403/2xx) and docs. The new role must not gain write access.
expectations: Constants contains the Reports policy/role and ConfigureAuth registers it with RequireRole plus the email assertion
The read endpoints for projects use the Reports policy or a policy that includes Reports; the write endpoints do not
The policy is mapped with CreateAuthorizedRouteGroupBuilder on a group that contains only read endpoints
TestUser has a Reports identity and TestUsers defines its fixed subject/email/role; the existing identities are preserved
local/tools/devtoken.json and local/openapi/users.json have a Reports profile/user with the same email and role
The authorization matrix covers anonymous 401, no-role 403, wrong-role 403, Reports 2xx on reads and 403 on writes
The agent ran the component tests and reported the real result
README API table and the local development docs mention the new role

evals.prompt: Review this working tree against the repository architecture and conventions. Report findings with severity and file:line; do not rewrite the code.
evals.expected_output: A review using references/review-checklist.md: hard-rule findings first (layer violation, SQL in the API, missing JSON context, test sleep), then judgement calls. Each finding cites the file, the rule and a one-line fix. The agent does not edit files.
expectations: The review identifies Application referencing Infrastructure as a blocker
The review identifies SQL built in an API handler (or a repository call from Api) as a blocker
The review identifies the new request/response missing from the feature JsonSerializerContext as a blocker or major finding
The review identifies Thread.Sleep/Task.Delay in a test as a blocker or major finding
Each finding cites file:line, the hard rule or judgement check, and a fix
The review distinguishes blockers, major findings and minor suggestions
The agent did not modify any file
The summary states what was not reviewed

evals.prompt: Remove the Todo sample feature from this repository. Keep the solution building and the local environment starting; remove its tests, SQL, seed and local examples.
evals.expected_output: An ordered removal: API surface and registrations, Application, Domain, Infrastructure, SQL/seed, tests, Tests.Shared Todo helpers, local OpenAPI examples, docs, and the architecture-test anchors. The agent runs the build, AOT publish, tests and a local start check.
expectations: The agent searched for every Todo reference before editing and reported the list
The API surface, OpenAPI tag/descriptors, JSON context, module registration and IGroupMap registration are removed
Application, Domain and Infrastructure Todo files are removed
The Todo SQL/seed is removed; db-init needs no change because it is feature-agnostic
The Todo tests and Tests.Shared helpers are removed; TestUser members that only existed for Todo are renamed or kept consistently
The local OpenAPI examples are removed; role profiles stay
The architecture-test anchors (typeof(TodoEntity), typeof(TodoRepository), typeof(TodoRoutes)) are replaced before the types are deleted
No orphan build error remains from a deleted type or a stale using
The agent ran build, AOT publish, tests and a local start check and reported the real results
